query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Altering the chemical composition of Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloys by a slight substitution (e.g., partial Co doping) can improve the magnetocaloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloys with known magneto-structural transition behavior.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled amount of Co doping to partially replace one of the constituent elements (likely Mn or In) to fine-tune the alloy’s transition characteristics.
generation.conditions: Measurements conducted near the martensitic transformation temperature (typically near room temperature) under a moderate magnetic field (approximately 2 Tesla).
generation.structural_mediator: Modification of the martensitic transformation characteristics and magnetic domain coupling due to chemical substitution.
generation.mechanism: The substitution is expected to enhance the magnetostructural coupling, increasing the magnetic entropy change during the phase transition, which in turn improves the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: An improved magnetocaloric performance, evidenced by a larger magnetic entropy change and/or adiabatic temperature change during the phase transformation, relative to the baseline Ni-Mn-In alloy composition.
generation.baseline: Standard Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloys without the additional doping.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is anticipated to occur only within an optimal window of doping level; excessive doping may dampen or suppress the martensitic transformation and the associated magnetocaloric effect.
generation.uncertainty: There is moderate uncertainty in determining the precise doping level required and the exact magnitude of performance improvement, as the coupling between structural and magnetic transitions is sensitive to minor compositional changes.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of Ni-Mn-In alloy samples with varying levels of controlled Co doping. For each sample, measure the magnetization, magnetic entropy change, and adiabatic temperature change around the expected martensitic transformation temperature under a magnetic field sweep (up to about 2 Tesla). Compare these measurements to a baseline sample without Co doping.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co doped samples do not exhibit at least a 10% improvement in ΔS_M or ΔT_ad compared to the baseline, or if the doping leads to significant suppression or elimination of the desired martensitic transformation, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
